messages:
Dave: heads-up - weird crash when running local sample. redwoodctl kept failing with 'invalid token file: unexpected end of JSON' after i enabled Dropbox sync for my home dir.

Meera: oh no. what did the error look like?

Dave: short log: 
```
$ redwoodctl status
Error: failed to load token file /Users/dave/.redwood/tokens/default.json: invalid character '\u0000' looking for beginning of value
```
I inspected the file and it was a zero-byte or truncated JSON half the time. Dropbox was doing a sync and left a `.dropbox.cache` temp or a `.file.part` around.

Oliver: this matches a class of issues where an external sync service briefly leaves partial files while uploading. If redwoodctl reads the token exactly at that moment you can get parse errors or zero-length files. Not an easy repro but happens enough with networked/synced homes.

Meera: thanks. two immediate mitigation ideas: 1) avoid recommending syncing `~/.redwood` in our quickstart; 2) make redwoodctl write tokens atomically (write tmp + fsync + rename) and validate json on load gracefully.

Dave: i can confirm atomic rename would have prevented the zero-byte case. in my case Dropbox sometimes creates `tokens/default.json.dropbox` and then moves it into place; but when it does a partial upload there was a moment where `default.json` was empty.

Oliver: implementation notes:
- write to `tokens/<profile>.json.tmp` then fsync parent dir and rename to `<profile>.json`
- on startup, if we see files with `.tmp` or `.dropbox*` or `~` suffixes, warn and ignore them rather than trying to parse
- add a quick recovery command: `redwoodctl tokens repair` that finds truncated files and restores from latest backup if available (or instructs user how to recover)

Meera: also add a doctor check: `redwoodctl doctor` should detect that REDWOOD_HOME is inside a known sync folder (Dropbox, GoogleDrive, OneDrive) by checking for presence of `.dropbox`, `Google Drive` mountpoints, etc., and warn: "Found REDWOOD_HOME inside Dropbox; file sync can cause token corruption. Consider excluding ~/.redwood from sync or set REDWOOD_HOME to a non-synced path."

Dave: docs change makes sense. our onboarding guide currently says "sync your dotfiles" and shows syncing your whole home for convenience. that's bad advice for sensitive credential dirs.

Oliver: long-term thought: add a lightweight journaling layer for tokens: keep `tokens/<profile>.json` plus `tokens/log-<ts>.json` appended event stream so we can recover last good token if current file is corrupt. But that's more invasive. Start with atomic write + ignore patterns + doctor warning.

Meera: also add log-level guidance: when parsing fails, we should not just print error and exit; print a friendly remediation: "This token file appears corrupt. If you use a file-sync service, try restoring from service history or move ~/.redwood out of sync. You can run `redwoodctl tokens list` to see available backups."

Dave: quick workaround i used: paused Dropbox sync, restored the file from Dropbox history, and set `REDWOOD_HOME=~/.redwood-local` for local runs. That unstuck me.

devex-bot: created issue #4012: "redwoodctl: avoid token corruption when REDWOOD_HOME is in a synced folder (Dropbox/Drive/OneDrive)" and assigned to @oliver for triage :spiral_note_pad:

Oliver: i'll pick this up. plan: 1) atomic write + unit tests simulating partial write 2) doctor detection + warning message 3) quickstart docs update + onboarding blurb to recommend excluding REDWOOD_HOME from sync 4) small `tokens repair` helper RFC after initial fixes land

ci-bot: scheduled CI job `devex/token-atomic-write` on oliver/atomic-token-write branch to run the new tests

Meera: can you also add a short note in the installer docs and the mac setup page? a lot of new hires use Dropbox for dotfiles.

Dave: thanks all. should save others from a scary "lost tokens" morning :)
